rows.observation: CFTC launched ANPRM for Regulation CTX (Crypto Asset Transactions) and Regulation CAM (Crypto Asset Markets) Oct 5; creates new Crypto Asset Market DCM subcategory for leveraged/margined retail crypto; requires FCM intermediation, DCO clearing, actual delivery test; 60-day comment period
research: "finding": "The CFTC published an Advanced Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (ANPRM) on October 5, 2026, titled 'Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets' (RIN 3038-AF80). The ANPRM proposes Regulation CTX to define when retail crypto asset transactions (CTXs) fall under CEA Section 2(c)(2)(D) and Regulation CAM to create a new 'crypto asset market' (CAM) subcategory of designated contract market (DCM) registration for venues offering leveraged, margined, or financed retail crypto transactions. The framework would require CTXs to be intermediated by futures commission merchants (FCMs) and cleared through derivatives clearing organizations (DCOs), with an 'actual delivery' exception for transfers of crypto assets to customer-controlled wallets within 28 days. A 60-day comment period runs from Federal Register publication.",

"evidence": "Multiple sources confirm the CFTC released the ANPRM on October 5, 2026 (Release 9307-26, RIN 3038-AF80). The ANPRM covers Regulation CTX (defining CTXs under CEA §2(c)(2)(D)) and Regulation CAM (creating a CAM subcategory of DCM). It requires FCM intermediation and DCO clearing for all CTXs, with leverage only through eligible providers under CAM rulebook arrangements. The 'actual delivery' test is based on customer possession/control (e.g., private keys) within 28 days per §2(c)(2)(D)(ii). Comments are due 60 days after Federal Register publication. The ANPRM is a preliminary step, not a final rule.",

rows.observation: ESMA MiCA stablecoin crackdown Oct 8: 3-month wind-down deadline Jan 8, 2027 for non-compliant ARTs/EMTs (USDT, PYUSD named); CASPs must not provide services; only narrow exit services permitted; no grandfathering; USDT $184B market cap still unauthorized in EU
research: "finding": "On 8 October 2026, ESMA published opinion ESMA75-113276571-1742 directing national competent authorities (NCAs) to require MiCA-authorised crypto-asset service providers (CASPs) to cease providing services related to non-MiCA-compliant asset-referenced tokens (ARTs) and e-money tokens (EMTs) — i.e., stablecoins that lack EU authorisation under MiCA Titles III/IV. CASPs must immediately block new EU-client acquisitions and limit existing services to a strictly supervised wind-down of legacy positions. NCAs should ensure remediation of remaining customer holdings as soon as possible and no later than three months after publication (8 January 2027). During the wind-down, only residual services such as liquidation, conversion, withdrawal, transfer, and safekeeping of existing holdings are permitted; new purchases, promotion, trading, active distribution, and continued market availability are prohibited. The opinion does not name specific tokens, but Tether’s USDT (market cap ~$184 billion) and PayPal USD (PYUSD) are widely identified as the largest unauthorised stablecoins affected. Private ownership and self-custody are not restricted; the measures apply only to services provided by MiCA-licensed firms. Enforcement timing and exact cut-off dates are left to individual NCAs, which may impose earlier deadlines within the three-month outer limit.",

"evidence": "Multiple authoritative sources (ESMA press releases, CoinDesk, Cointelegraph, CryptoPotato, EU AlphaPilot, Finobird, etc.) consistently report the 8 October 2026 ESMA opinion (ESMA75-113276571-1742) setting a three-month wind-down period ending 8 January 2027 for non-MiCA-compliant ARTs/EMTs. The opinion covers the full range of MiCA Title V services (trading, exchange, order execution, custody, transfers, advice, portfolio management). It explicitly rejects investor warnings as sufficient and brings custody/transfers into scope, unlike the January 2025 guidance. USDT (~$184 B) and PYUSD are repeatedly cited as the most prominent unauthorised tokens. Sources confirm no grandfathering, only narrow exit services, and that enforcement is delegated to NCAs.",

rows.observation: CLARITY Act stalled in Senate (Sep 15 cloture failure 49-50); ethics impasse on presidential crypto divestiture; Senate recess until Nov 9; unlikely to pass this Congress; agencies filling vacuum via CFTC rulemaking and SEC innovation exemption
research: "finding": "The CLARITY Act (H.R. 3633) failed to advance in the Senate when cloture on the motion to proceed was rejected 49-50 on September 15, 2026, falling 11 votes short of the 60-vote threshold, with all 49 'yeas' from Republicans and 50 'nays' including 44 Democrats, 2 independents, and 4 Republicans, leaving the bill stalled with the Senate recessed until November 9 and unlikely to pass the 119th Congress, prompting the CFTC and SEC to fill the regulatory vacuum through agency rulemaking and exemptions.",

"evidence": "On September 15, 2026, the Senate voted 49-50 on cloture on the motion to proceed to H.R. 3633 (the CLARITY Act) at 2:19 PM, with 60 votes required, falling 11 votes short. The 49 yeas were all Republicans; the 50 nays were 44 Democrats, 2 independents (King and Sanders), and 4 Republicans (Collins, Hawley, Moran, Tillis). Senator Chris Coons (D) did not vote (1 not voting). The vote was procedural, ending debate on whether to take up the bill, not a vote on the bill itself. The bill passed the House 294-134 on July 17, 2025. The Senate had filed the cloture motion on August 8, 2026. Senators Collins, Hawley, Moran, and Tillis voted no; Tillis switched to no to file a motion to reconsider at 3:01 PM the same day. The failure was driven by an ethics impasse over presidential crypto divestiture, specifically concerns about President Trump's $1.4 billion in crypto earnings from World Liberty Financial and the TRUMP memecoin, with Democrats refusing to support a bill they argued did not go far enough to restrict officials' crypto interests. With the Senate scheduled to return on November 9, 2026, and the 119th Congress nearing its end on December 18, 2026, the bill is unlikely to pass this Congress. In the wake of the failure, the CFTC submitted a rulemaking titled 'Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets' (RIN 3038-AF80) to the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs on September 17, 2026, and the SEC issued an Innovation Exemption (Release No. 34-106402) on the same day, granting five-year temporary exemptive relief to Tokenized Securities Venues (TSVs) to facilitate onchain trading of tokenized NMS stocks, with SEC Chairman Paul Atkins explicitly tying the action to the CLARITY Act's failure.",

"context": "The CLARITY Act, which would have established the first comprehensive U.S. federal regulatory framework for digital assets by splitting oversight between the SEC and CFTC, faced its decisive procedural test on September 15, 2026, when Senate cloture on the motion to proceed failed 49-50, 11 votes short of the 60-vote threshold needed under Senate Rule XXII. The bill had previously passed the House 294-134 on July 17, 2025, and cleared the Senate Banking Committee 15-9 on May 14, 2026, but stalled on the Senate floor primarily due to an ethics impasse centered on President Trump's extensive crypto holdings—including his 38% stake in World Liberty Financial and proceeds from the TRUMP memecoin, which generated approximately $1.4 billion in 2025 income. The bill's lead Republican sponsors, including Senator Cynthia Lummis, had argued that recent revisions incorporated 126 substantive changes requested by Democrats, including expanded ethics language, but Senate Democrats unanimously opposed it, with the seven key Democratic negotiators citing insufficient conflict-of-interest protections. The vote breakdown revealed a clean partisan divide: all 49 'yeas' were Republicans, while 50 'nays' included 44 Democrats, 2 independents, and 4 Republicans (Collins, Hawley, Moran, and Tillis)—the latter of whom switched to 'no' specifically to preserve a motion to reconsider. With the Senate scheduled to remain in pro forma session until November 9, 2026, and the 119th Congress scheduled to adjourn on December 18, 2026, the bill's prospects for passage this Congress are considered highly unlikely, leaving a regulatory vacuum that the SEC and CFTC have moved to fill through agency action.",

The claim that agencies are 'filling the vacuum' is substantiated by the SEC's Innovation Exemption issued on September 17, 2026, and the CFTC's submission of its crypto asset rulemaking to OIRA on the same date, though the full scope and timeline of these agency initiatives remains uncertain. "context": "Securitize launched its Securitize Stocks product on October 8, 2026, bringing 12 major U.S. equities — including Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Alphabet, Tesla, Meta, Amazon, Netflix, Circle, Strategy, Palantir, and SpaceX — onto the Solana blockchain.
